newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street seen opening up on sales data.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street seen opening up on sales data.

text.p: Wall Street markets should open higher Tuesday on retail sales data that was largely in line with expectations, analysts said.
They said the figures might ease the pressure on the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates at the May 20 meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee.
"Bonds should show some improvement on these figures and the market will likely continue on its merry way," said Alan Ackerman, market strategist at Fahnestock & Co.
April retail sales fell 0.3 percent overall, in line with economists' consensus estimate. Excluding autos, sales fell 0.1 percent, below the estimate of a 0.1 percent rise.
"The market will probably open higher, particularly with the retail figures," said Stanley Nabi, vice chairman of Wood Struthers & Winthrop and chairman of its investment policy panel.

Pierre Ellis, senior economist at Primark Decision Research, said, "The data is very moderate for the economy, which is what the Fed wants to see. It reduces the odds of a rate tightening, which the markets should like."
The U.S. Treasury 30-year bond was up 6/32 to yield 6.87. The Standard & Poors 500 futures index was up 0.45 to 841.80.
